jobs.title: Projektleiter (d/m/w) Anlagenbau
jobs.description: Deine Aufgaben Als Projektleiter (d/m/w) Anlagenbau in unserem Geschäftsbereich Wasserbehandlung setzt du in einem dynamischen Team innovative Lösungen für unsere Kunden weltweit um. Zu deinen Aufgaben gehören unter anderem: Fachliche und administrative Leitung nationaler und internationaler Anlagenbauprojekte Verantwortung für den gesamten Projektverlauf – von der Planung bis zur Inbetriebnahme Mitwirkung bei der Erstellung von Angeboten und bei Vertragsverhandlungen Zentrale Ansprechperson für unsere Kunden, Projektteams und weitere Projektbeteiligte Steuerung, Koordination und Kontrolle interner und externer Projektbeteiligter Mitwirkung bei der Ressourcen-, Termin- und Kapazitätsplanung Laufendes Projektreporting und -controlling Überwachung von Projektzielen, Budgets, Terminen und Qualitätsanforderungen Frühzeitige Identifikation und Klärung von Zielkonflikten Transparente Information der Auftraggebenden über Projektfortschritt, Risiken und offene Entscheidungen Dein Profil Als Projektleiter (d/m/w) Anlagenbau Wasserbehandlung bringst du folgende Qualifikationen und Fähigkeiten mit: Abgeschlossenes Studium, zum Beispiel in Wasserwirtschaft, Verfahrenstechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im industriellen Anlagenbau Erfahrung in der Leitung oder Steuerung von Projekten sowie sicherer Umgang mit gängigen Projektmanagementmethoden und -tools Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Selbstständige, strukturierte und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise Ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Koordinationsfähigkeit Fähigkeit, unterschiedliche Interessen zusammenzuführen und Entscheidungen klar vorzubereiten Bereitschaft zu weltweiten Dienstreisen Führerschein der Klasse B Wir bieten Als Teil unseres Teams bei DAS Environmental Expert GmbH bieten wir dir: Karriere & individuelle Entwicklung: Deine berufliche Entwicklung gestalten wir gemeinsam. Individuelle Karrierewege orientieren sich an deinen Stärken, Interessen und fachlichen Schwerpunkten. Weiterbildung & fachliche Tiefe: Ein vielseitiges Weiterbildungsprogramm ergänzt dein abwechslungsreiches Aufgabengebiet und ermöglicht dir, dein technisches Know-how kontinuierlich auszubauen. Abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben & Projekte: Du arbeitest an vielfältigen Aufgaben im Tagesgeschäft und bringst dich aktiv in Projekte ein. Dabei kannst du Ideen einbringen, technische Probleme lösen und Innovationen vorantreiben. Faire Vergütung: Wir bieten dir eine faire Entlohnung, die Qualifikation, Verantwortung und Leistung angemessen berücksichtigt. Flexible Arbeitszeiten & mobiles Arbeiten: Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten schaffst du dir Raum für konzentriertes, produktives Arbeiten – ideal für kreative Lösungsansätze, komplexe technische Fragestellungen und eine gute Balance im Alltag. Moderne Arbeitsplätze & Coworking Spaces: Moderne, ergonomische Arbeitsplätze und Coworking-Spaces bieten dir optimale Bedingungen für konzentriertes Arbeiten sowie für Projekt- und Teamarbeit. Eine zeitgemäße technische Ausstattung und das passende Equipment stellen wir dir selbstverständlich zur Verfügung. Sinnstiftende Arbeit & Nachhaltigkeit: Bei uns arbeitest du an Lösungen, die Luft und Wasser schützen und industrielle Prozesse nachhaltiger machen. So leistest du mit deiner Arbeit einen aktiven Beitrag zum Umwelt- und Ressourcenschutz und gestaltest eine grüne Zukunft mit. Teamarbeit & Du-Kultur: Flache Hierarchien, kurze Entscheidungswege und eine gelebte Du-Kultur fördern Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe und echtes Teamwork. Work-Life-Balance: Mit unserer 38-Stunden-Woche, flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen und Gleitzeit – sowie, wenn es die Tätigkeit erlaubt, mobilem Arbeiten – unterstützen wir dich dabei, Beruf und Privatleben gut miteinander zu vereinbaren. Zusätzlich profitierst du von 30 Tagen Urlaub sowie Zusatzurlaub nach Betriebszugehörigkeit. Du suchst ab sofort eine neue, unbefristete Herausforderung und die beschriebenen Aufgaben sind genau das Richtige für dich? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung!

jobs.description: jobDescription: Wir suchen übergreifend an den Standorten Denzlingen und Freiburg-Hochdorf in unserem Bereich Personal-Ausbildung dich als Auszubildenden zum Verfahrenstechnologe Metall (m/w/d) mit Ausbildungsbeginn Herbst 2027. Du wirst aktiv in die abwechslungsreichen Tätigkeiten eingebunden, darfst eigenverantwortlich mitarbeiten und somit bereits in der Ausbildung deine eigenen Ideen einbringen. In unseren zahlreichen Seminaren und Ausbildungsprojekten kannst du deine Eigenverantwortlichkeit, Kreativität und Teamfähigkeit unter Beweis stellen. Auch Auslandseinsätze in einer unserer Landesgesellschaften sind möglich. Berufsschule: Gewerbliche Schule in Kehl/Rhein Die Kosten für die Unterbringung im Schülerwohnheim sowie die Fahrtkosten werden von der Unternehmensgruppe fischer übernommen Schwerpunkte: Wirtschaftskompetenz, Berufsfachliche Kompetenz, Projektkompetenz qualifications: Hauptschulabschluss Interesse an Technik, Metallbearbeitung, Steuerungstechnik (Pneumatik / Elektropneumatik) Weitere Informationen findest du auf unserer Ausbildungshomepage. additionalInformation: Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung über unser Online-Bewerbungsformular. jobs.title: PMO Coordinator
jobs.description: WHO WE ARE Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant. Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach. Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions. BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO - Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them. - Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology. - Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world. - Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck. YOUR IMPACT You’re the reason the PMO’s reporting rhythm runs on time, every time, so no function lead is left scrambling for a last-minute slide the night before a gate review. You bring cost, schedule and risk inputs together into one clear, decision-ready picture for leadership, and you chase the gaps early, before they turn into someone else’s problem in the room. You’re also the fabric of the PMO. This goes well beyond reporting: you’ll help us make sense of the data we collect, creating unexpected insights, pointing out unseen opportunities and uncovering hidden dependencies. You’ll bring fresh ideas on how we work and challenge how things have always been done, and your insights will shape the decisions that move Alpha forward. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Own the PMO's reporting cadence, pulling together inputs from the Cost Controller, Programme Schedule Manager and Risk & Change Manager into steering committee packs and gate-readiness reports - Chase status updates ahead of gate reviews and leadership meetings, flagging anything missing, out of date or inconsistent before it reaches a decision forum - Maintain the reporting templates and dashboards (in Wrike or similar) that give leadership a clear view of milestones and status - Keep the master calendar of programme deliverables, gates and milestones across Alpha and Stellaris up to date - Support the logistics for PMO governance forums, including the Release Gates Authority and steering committees, from scheduling to papers - Help with ad hoc analysis of cost, schedule and risk data to support PMO decisions WHO YOU ARE - You've supported a PMO or project controls function on a complex, multi-discipline programme, and you know what it takes to keep many moving parts in view - You're highly organised and good at turning input from engineers, suppliers and commercial teams into reporting that's clear, concise and actually gets read - You're confident with project management and reporting tools, and you pick up new ones quickly - You're fluent in English; German is a plus - You enjoy building things that don't exist yet and are comfortable with the pace and ambiguity that comes with it - You get real satisfaction from being the connective tissue of a programme: making progress, risks and dependencies visible so the people making decisions can make good ones INTERVIEW PROCESS - Recruiter Interview (30-60 min) - Technical Screening (60 min) - Technical Panel (2x60 min) At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

jobs.description: ÜBER UNS Vertanical – A World free of Chronic Pain. Dabei verfolgen wir eine klare Vision: Eine Welt frei von chronischen Schmerzen! Mit VER-01 haben wir ein einzigartiges cannabinoidbasiertes Arzneimittel zur Behandlung chronischer Schmerzen entwickelt, das im Juni 2026 unter dem Namen Exilby in Deutschland und Österreich zugelassen wurde. Damit haben wir nach mehr als acht Jahren intensiver Forschungs- und Entwicklungsarbeit einen bedeutenden Meilenstein erreicht. Die Zulassung in den USA ist für 2029 geplant. Dann bewirb Dich jetzt! Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen. DEINE MISSION BEI UNS Gestalte die Zukunft der Schmerztherapie mit uns! Als kreativer Kopf hinter bahnbrechenden klinischen Studien übernimmst Du nicht nur Verantwortung für Design, Durchführung und Datenanalyse, sondern führst ein engagiertes Team von Experten zum Erfolg. In dieser Schlüsselrolle bist Du der Motor für Innovationen und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Vision einer schmerzfreien Welt Realität wird. Bist Du bereit, Prozesse neu zu denken und Studien auf ein neues Level zu heben? Dann suchen wir genau Dich! DEINE AUFGABEN - Du übernimmst die operative Verantwortung für die Bereiche Medical Writing, Data Management, Biostatistics, Programming, Medical Monitoring und Clinical Safety in direkter Berichtslinie an die Geschäftsführung. - Du führst ein hochmotiviertes Team von insgesamt 12 Mitarbeitenden disziplinarisch und entwickelst diese gezielt weiter. - Du designst klinische Studien, definierst die Anforderungen an Datenerfassung und -auswertung und verantwortest sowohl die Datenqualität als auch die Sicherheit der Patienten. - Du verantwortest die Erstellung des klinischen Dossiers für Marktzulassungsanträge und koordinierst die Kommunikation mit den Behörden bei Rückfragen. - Du entwickelst die strategische Ausrichtung des klinischen Studienprogramms weiter – einschließlich der Bewertung und Auswahl neuer Indikationen. - Du bist federführend verantwortlich für die Auswahl und Steuerung externer Dienstleister inklusive der Verhandlung von Projektbudgets. - Du verantwortest und optimierst Prozesse in Deinen Bereichen und entwickelst das Organisationszielbild stetig weiter. DEIN PROFIL - Du verfügst über ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes MS-/MA-, M.D.- oder PhD-Studium in Naturwissenschaften, Medizin, Pharmazie oder einer vergleichbaren Studienrichtung. - Du hast mindestens 6–8 Jahre Berufserfahrung gesammelt – idealerweise in einer Top-Strategieberatung oder in einem dynamischen Start-up-Umfeld. - Deine sehr guten analytischen Fähigkeiten verbindest Du mit einer ergebnisorientierten und detailgenauen Arbeitsweise. - Du kommunizierst klar, strukturiert und überzeugend – auf unterschiedlichen Ebenen und mit verschiedenen Ansprechpartner:innen. - Du denkst strategisch, übernimmst Verantwortung und hast Freude daran, Strukturen und Prozesse aktiv weiterzuentwickeln. - Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse runden Dein Profil ab. UNSER VERSPRECHEN Wir setzen Dinge um – und das schnell! Dich erwartet ein Top-Management-Board von hochklassigen Unternehmern, früheren Beratern und erfahrenen Industrie-Größen. Wir bieten Dir das Umfeld, in dem Du Dich persönlich und beruflich beispiellos weiterentwickeln kannst. Du hast Rückfragen? jobs.title: Produktionsmitarbeiter (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Deine Aufgaben: In dieser Rolle bist du ein wesentlicher Teil unseres Produktionsteams, bedienst Anlagen und stellst höchste Qualitätsstandards für unsere innovativen pflanzlichen Fleischprodukte sicher. Du arbeitest in einer sauberen, modernen Produktionsumgebung, in der deine Detailgenauigkeit und dein Engagement für Lebensmittelsicherheit direkt zu unserer Mission beitragen, die Lebensmittelindustrie zu transformieren. Hauptaufgaben Produktionsbetrieb: Bedienung von Produktionsanlagen und Maschinen gemäß festgelegter Verfahren und Sicherheitsprotokolle. Überwachung der Produktionsprozesse, um gleichbleibende Produktqualität und Einhaltung der Produktionsziele sicherzustellen. Qualitätskontrolle: Durchführung von Qualitätskontrollen während des gesamten Produktionsprozesses, einschließlich Sichtprüfungen und Basistests. Unverzügliche Meldung von Qualitätsproblemen oder Abweichungen von den Spezifikationen an Vorgesetzte. Lebensmittelsicherheit & Hygiene: Einhaltung strenger Lebensmittelsicherheitsprotokolle und Aufrechterhaltung hoher Hygienestandards zu jeder Zeit. Befolgung von HACCP-Verfahren, Sanitäranforderungen und Richtlinien für persönliche Schutzausrüstung (PSA). Anlagenwartung: Durchführung grundlegender Reinigungs- und Wartungsarbeiten an Anlagen nach Anweisung. Unverzügliche Meldung von Anlagenstörungen, ungewöhnlichen Geräuschen oder Leistungsproblemen an die Wartungsteams. Materialhandhabung: Handhabung von Rohstoffen, Zutaten und Fertigprodukten gemäß festgelegter Verfahren. Einhaltung ordnungsgemäßer Lagerbedingungen und Sicherstellung korrekter Kennzeichnung und Dokumentation. Dein Profil: Wenn du eine Leidenschaft für Lebensmittelproduktion hast und Teil der Herstellung revolutionärer pflanzlicher Fleischprodukte sein möchtest, ist dies deine Chance, zu einer bahnbrechenden Produktion beizutragen und gleichzeitig wertvolle Fähigkeiten in einem schnell wachsenden, werteorientierten Startup aufzubauen. Anforderungen Erfahrung: Vorherige Erfahrung in der Lebensmittelproduktion, Fertigung oder einem verwandten industriellen Umfeld bevorzugt, aber nicht erforderlich. Wir begrüßen Kandidaten, die bereit sind, zu lernen und mit unserem Team zu wachsen. Arbeitsanforderungen: Diese Position erfordert längeres Stehen, Handhabung von Materialien bis zu 25 kg und Arbeit in einer temperaturkontrollierten Umgebung. Manuelle Geschicklichkeit ist für die Bedienung von Anlagen und die Handhabung von Materialien erforderlich. Wir begrüßen Bewerbungen von allen qualifizierten Kandidaten und werden angemessene Anpassungen im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Vorgaben prüfen. Technische Fähigkeiten: Grundlegendes Verständnis von Lebensmittelsicherheitsprinzipien und Hygienepraktiken. Fähigkeit, detaillierte schriftliche und mündliche Anweisungen zu befolgen. Grundlegende Computerkenntnisse für Dateneingabe und Aufzeichnungen. Bereitschaft, den Betrieb von Anlagen und Produktionsprozessen zu erlernen. Soziale Kompetenzen: Ausgeprägte Detailgenauigkeit und Engagement für Qualität. Zuverlässige Arbeitsethik mit der Fähigkeit, selbstständig und im Team zu arbeiten. Flexibilität, bei Bedarf in verschiedenen Schichten zu arbeiten. Sicherheitsbewusstsein: Verständnis von Arbeitsplatzsicherheitsprinzipien und Engagement für die Einhaltung von Sicherheitsprotokollen. Bereitschaft, erforderliche PSA zu tragen und eine saubere Arbeitsumgebung zu pflegen. Sprachkenntnisse: Deutschkenntnisse erforderlich für Sicherheitskommunikation und das Befolgen von Anweisungen. Grundlegende Englischkenntnisse von Vorteil für internationale Teaminteraktionen. Warum wir?: Warum du dich jetzt bewerben solltest Großes Wachstum: Wir befinden uns an einem spannenden Wendepunkt und wechseln von einer Pilotphase zur Skalierung des Betriebs. Sei Teil von etwas Transformativem und baue es von Grund auf mit auf. Erstklassige Unterstützung: Wir werden von erstklassigen VCs und Angels unterstützt, die unsere Vision teilen und an unsere Mission glauben. Jetzt ist die Zeit: Die Lebensmittelindustrie braucht eine massive Transformation. Begleite uns dabei, unwiderstehliche, nachhaltige Lebensmittel zu kreieren, die Milliarden dazu inspirieren, schnell von tierischem Fleisch umzusteigen! Ein Wort zu Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Wir setzen uns für Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit für alle ein. Gemeinsame Werte und die Identifikation mit dem Zweck von Project Eaden sind uns am wichtigsten. Wir begrüßen Bewerbungen von allen qualifizierten Kandidaten, unabhängig von Alter, Hautfarbe, nationaler Herkunft, Rasse, Religion, Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Geschlechtsidentität oder Familienstand. Arbeitsplatz und Kultur Wir bauen etwas Massives auf – einen sanften Riesen in der Lebensmittelindustrie. Unser Team lebt von Zusammenarbeit, und wir glauben an die Kraft der persönlichen Kommunikation, um schnell und effektiv zu arbeiten. Derzeit verbringen wir die meiste Zeit gemeinsam an unserem Arbeitsplatz in Berlin, um unseren Teamgeist und unsere Kultur zu pflegen. Während wir in den nächsten Jahren wachsen, streben wir danach, uns zu einem stärker verteilten Arbeitsplatz zu entwickeln, der die Flexibilität von Remote-Arbeit mit der Stärke unserer gemeinsamen Werte und Verbundenheit verbindet.

jobs.title: Electrical Test Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description: 🌍 BUILD THE FUTURE OF CLIMATE TECH WITH PHLAIR We're solving humanity's biggest challenge, and it takes everything we've got. The world needs more energy, not less. Fossil fuels powered our economy for decades, at the cost of our planet. At Phlair, we're inverting that equation with breakthrough electrochemical Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology that pulls CO₂ from the air for permanent storage or repurposing into carbon-negative chemicals. We're not here to play it safe. We're here to win. WHY WE’RE DIFFERENT? We solve hard problems and are product-first. Our hydrolyzer-based Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology, enabling scalable and low-cost CO2 capture from ambient air. The electrochemical technology allows off-the-shelf components and is ideally suited to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources. With proven offtake agreements from customers such as Google, McKinsey, JPMorganChase, Shopify, Stripe, H&M, and Deep Sky; we're one of only seven DAC companies with real market validation. Project Dawn isn't just our flagship; it's our shot to scale CO₂ removal globally. IS THIS A FIT FOR ME? We're building for the 3-5% who are energized by winning and thrive under pressure. Our pace demands people who see excellence as non-negotiable and execution as everything. We cherish work-life-harmony, not balance. If you need extensive structure or prefer playing it safe, we're probably not the right fit. Don't tick every box? We value potential and spikes over perfect resumes. If you believe you can contribute to our mission at this intensity level, tell us why. YOUR MISSION - Test Plan Development: Collaborate with our CSO Steffen https://www.linkedin.com/in/steffen-garbe-017425143/ to design and execute tests for evaluating the functionality and compliance of our electrochemical stack for our 260 tCO2/year DAC demonstrator. - Collaborate: Work with the team to develop internal and external test setups. - Infrastructure Setup & Maintenance: Set up and maintain the test infrastructure, with a focus on quality assurance and reliability. Electrical wiring qualifications are a plus. - Data Analysis: Analyze test data and communicate key results to the development team. - Adapt & Innovate: In the fast-paced startup world, your ability to adapt to an evolving environment and quickly pivot will be crucial. You’ll work autonomously, learn on the go, and contribute to shaping a new sector. Your targets are your North Star. Nothing is set in stone in our world, we adapt fast, but we always hit our goals. WHAT YOU BRING - Education: M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering. - Testing Experience: Experience designing and conducting test protocols. - Electrochemical Testing: Familiarity with cell stack testing - fuel cells, electrolysers, flow batteries, electrodialysers or similar. - Data Skills: Strong in data analysis and presenting results clearly. ESSENTIAL TRAITS - Methodical & Detail-Oriented - You work carefully and focus on the details - Troubleshooter - You identify issues and maintain test stands - Bias for action - You prototype, test, and ship while others are still planning - Comfortable with intensity - 12-hour days and weekend sprints don't scare you, they energize you - Ego second - You care more about winning than being right - Figure things out independently - No hand-holding. You own problems end-to-end - Excellence as standard - Mistakes happen, but mediocrity doesn't BONUS POINTS - Test Automation: Basic scripting knowledge (LabVIEW, Matlab, Python, R-Studio). - Electronics Qualification: Formal qualification in electronics for high-voltage DC/AC HOW WE WORK In-person matters: We work fully onsite in Ismaning, Germany. Our pilot plant is here, our breakthroughs happen here, and our team wins here—together. Goals matter: We do everything to achieve our goals. If your workstream is the bottleneck, you don't stop. This isn't about serving hours, it's about hitting goals that matter. Leadership means showing up and doing the work. We get that experienced people have more commitments, but championship teams require championship effort. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive salary and stock options to share in the company’s success - 30 vacation days - Public transport pass for all of Germany - Relocation support to help you settle into Munich - Fitness and wellness benefits to keep you at your best - Fresh team lunches, prepared by our amazing chef, Amelie - Direct leadership access to our CEO, CTO, and CSO 🔗 LEARN MORE ABOUT PHLAIR - Our Mission, Vision and Team https://phlair.com/careers - Phlair Secures Frontier’s First Electrochemical DAC Deal https://frontierclimate.com/writing/phlair - Technology Behind Phlair https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/19/phlairs-carbon-sucking-technology-could-lower-direct-air-captures-costs/ - The Future of DAC https://medium.com/extantia-capital/will-direct-air-capture-ever-be-affordable-the-rise-of-dac-3-0-d46cb355f35c ------ We're committed to building a high-performing team where exceptional people can do their best work. Our hiring process is designed to identify those who thrive in demanding environments while ensuring fair consideration for all qualified candidates.

jobs.title: Automation Engineer, Wet Lab
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY: At Differential Bio, our mission is to unlock the potential of the bioeconomy by fixing how biological R&D and scale-up are done. Today, bioprocess development is slow, expensive, and limited by the economics of lab hardware. A typical system runs 4, 8, or 24 bioreactors in parallel, and a single run can cost anywhere from hundreds to several thousand dollars. Our ambition is different: 100 parallel bioreactor runs at around $10 per run. Why does that matter? Because radically reducing the cost per insight changes what is possible. Instead of running a handful of carefully selected experiments, we can generate dense, standardized datasets across thousands of conditions. That data is at the core of Differential Bio. First, we automate high-throughput data generation. Then we use our proprietary datasets to train AI models that understand how bioprocesses behave across conditions and scales - with the long-term goal of building a digital twin of fermentation at any scale. We have already built two end-to-end automated fermentation pods that operate continuously and generate experimental data every week. Being vertically integrated all the way down to the physical lab has proven to be a major advantage for us. Now we are hiring the first role dedicated entirely to lab automation. You will take over this domain from our founder and CTO, Martin, report directly to him, and own how our automation platform develops from here. This is, in many ways, the role we always wished existed: high autonomy, genuinely difficult engineering problems, the freedom and resources to solve them properly, and a mission worth the hard work. This is not a role for someone who wants to select the next six-figure laboratory automation system from a catalogue. We want someone who looks at a €500,000 solution and asks: Why does this cost €500,000? What problem are we actually solving? And could we achieve the same outcome - or a better one - for a fraction of the cost and at 10x the scale? Sometimes the answer will be an established lab instrument. Sometimes it will be an industrial robot, a €50 sensor, a 3D-printed part, and some clever engineering. Your opportunity is to help us completely rethink how lab automation is done and build the infrastructure that makes biological R&D dramatically faster and cheaper. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: - Own lab automation at Differential Bio end-to-end, from creating individual components to developing complete new automated fermentation systems, including technical decisions, experimentation, suppliers, and budget. - Drive our ambition to dramatically increase experimental density while reducing the cost per experiment and cost per insight. - Translate wet-lab workflows into reliable, scalable automation together with our scientists, software engineers, and ML engineers. - Make pragmatic build vs. buy vs. modify decisions instead of defaulting to expensive, closed laboratory automation platforms. - Prototype and build yourself: fermentation pods and small bioreactors, using 3D printing & our workshop. - Evaluate and integrate robots, liquid handling systems, and emerging automation technologies, working directly with manufacturers to adapt or co-develop around our requirements. - Continuously improve reliability, throughput, maintainability, and cost as our automation platform scales. QUALIFICATIONS: We care more about how you solve engineering problems than about a specific degree or career path. You should: - Have evidence of excellence: 4+ years of experience in lab automation, robotics, or other automation projects involving real hardware - or an equivalent track record of serious hobby projects where you have built, modified, automated, and debugged physical systems yourself. - Be a tinkerer: someone who enjoys opening the box, understanding how something works, modifying it, and building something better when necessary. - Be comfortable with robotics, sensors, actuators, mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, or related technologies. - Be able to move quickly between disciplines and collaborate with wet-lab scientists, automation specialists, software engineers, and ML engineers. - Be comfortable with ambiguity and high autonomy. We define outcomes; you have substantial freedom to determine how to achieve them. - Combine creative engineering with a strong focus on reliability and repeatability. Experience with laboratory automation, bioreactors, liquid handling, CAD, 3D printing, Python, PLCs, machine vision, or industrial automation is a plus - but not a requirement. This is a demanding job. The problems are hard, the ownership is real, and there will not always be a playbook to follow. We are looking for someone who enjoys that responsibility rather than avoids it. We want to see the fire in you: the curiosity, energy, and determination to keep digging until something works. BENEFITS: - Build something fundamentally new: Help move lab automation away from boutique, over-engineered systems toward high-density biological data factories. - High ownership: Own our lab automation stack, technical direction, suppliers, and significant parts of the automation budget. - Real freedom to build: We have 3D printers, workshop capabilities, testing space, and the budget to buy robots and hardware when experimentation requires it. - Direct impact: Work closely with our founder and CTO and shape one of Differential Bio's core technological advantages. - Competitive compensation through salary + stock options. - eGym WellPass membership.

jobs.title: Senior Scientist, Upstream Fermentation R&D
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY: We’re hiring a Senior Scientist, Upstream Fermentation R&D to build out Differential’s wet lab capabilities and help deliver customer projects in various domains, ranging from Probiotics to Specialty Chemicals. You will drive delivery across a growing pipeline of customer projects end-to-end, from scoping research and project plans to hands-on assay development and microbiology work, all while managing time, budget, and quality. In close collaboration with lab automation and bioinformatics, you’ll define scalable, model-ready workflows and develop the methods, instrumentation, and tools that make them reliable in production. You will design and run media and cultivation experiments, develop assays, and generate AI-ready datasets to drive data-driven optimizations across a range of industrially relevant microbes and applications. You’ll work closely with our existing microbiology team, help scale it further, and coach junior team members on experimental execution, documentation standards, and reproducibility. You share our vision and actively evangelize data/AI/robotics-driven media and bioprocess optimization as the engine of the Bioeconomy’s Future. If this is you, apply and tell us how you’ll put it into practice. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: - Lead cultivation and study of a broad range of microbial species, from our current focus on lactic acid bacteria to industry workhorses such as E. coli, P. pastoris, and B. subtilis; also handle strains with challenging traits. - Develop media to enhance productivity and stability at lab scale, with the potential (not required) to extend into bioprocess development (e.g., feeding strategies, temperature, pH) at lab and production scale. - Design, validate, and standardize assays that inform media/bioprocess choices and support strain characterization, functional testing, and QC. - Translate customer requirements into lean, milestone-driven scientific research plans that optimize speed, cost, and decision quality in a resource-conscious startup environment. - Collaborate with lab automation and data science teams to design scalable, model-ready data capture for fermentation parameters and metabolite panels. - Lead and develop junior scientists/technicians to execute experiments precisely and maintain rigorous documentation, enforcing SOP/QA standards. QUALIFICATIONS: - Ph.D. (or equivalent work experience) in Microbiology or related field - 3+ years in industrial or translational research in microbial fermentation (probiotics/(agri)food/cosmetics preferred). - Proven ownership and hands-on experience in cultivation and media development across lactid acid bacteria, B. subtilis, E. coli, and yeasts in an industrial/bioprocess setting; exposure to challenging traits (fastidious, anaerobic) is a plus. Strong depth in at least one is sufficient. - Assay developer at heart with demonstrated design/validation of microbiology assays. - Demonstrated ownership with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, resource-constrained research environment, proven judgment on time/budget trade-offs (build vs. buy, lab infrastructure, lean experimentation) to optimize speed, cost, and decision quality. - Excellent written and verbal communication in English - clear stakeholder updates, customer presentations, and concise technical writing. - Regular, in-person presence at our Freising campus or downtown Munich lab is required. NICE-TO-HAVE: - Hands-on experience with benchtop bioreactors; huge plus if you have demonstrated scale-up experience, from lab to production-scale. - Experience with obligate anaerobes and otherwise challenging strains, e.g. handling fastidious, flocculent, agglutinating, sporulating strains, and working with nutritionally demanding or slow-growing microbes. - Proven cross-functional project management across wetlab and automation/bioinformatics/bioprocess workstreams. - Experience with Python/R/Matlab for DoE, growth/fermentation analytics, modeling-ready datasets, and light scripting; reads/writes instrument CSV/API and LIMS fields. - Having already demonstrated a builder mindset, experience shipping in a startup or through internal research projects; comfortable with ambiguity and end-to-end ownership. BENEFITS: - High autonomy to steer scientific development, deliver ambitiously, and help build a high-performing team - be a cornerstone hire. - State-of-the-art labs in Freising and Munich (Martinsried) with a central Munich office (close to the Central Station). - Competitive salary + meaningful stock options. - eGym WellPass membership.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Data Scientist
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY: At Differential Bio, our mission is to unlock the potential of the bioeconomy by fixing how biological R&D and scale-up are done. We’re looking for a Machine Learning Data Scientist to join our growing cutting-edge modelling team. You will develop novel machine learning algorithms and mechanistic models of bioprocess systems and push them from research proof-of-concept into production-ready commercial use. This role is focused on research, including creating hybrid models that combine mechanistic and machine learning approaches to predict how microbial fermentations behave, and that keep working when we move to a new organism, a new sensor, or a larger reactor. You’ll play an instrumental role on two existing grants and work with leading academic groups and industrial partners on pilot- and production-scale data. In addition, you’ll develop new research projects and drive them to completion and application on customer projects. We’re interested in researchers who want their work to end up in real bioreactors and are excited about working at an early-stage startup. You should be comfortable owning hard, open-ended problems where nobody has the answer yet, making evidence-based decisions under uncertainty, and shipping real solutions. How you’ll work - You’ll collaborate with technical leads and academic/industry external partners to design and execute research that meets our commitments in both consortia and strengthens our own platform. - You’ll own your research projects from scoping to delivery, with support from our modelling lead but with autonomy and independence. - You’ll work closely with our wet lab, dry lab and software teams, and identify which data you need to generate from our robotic lab. - You can work remotely, provided you’re based within ±2 hours of Central European Time (CET), with occasional travel KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Hybrid bioprocess modelling - Develop hybrid mechanistic/ML cell response models that predict fermentation outcomes (growth, titer, yield, productivity) from process and sensor data. - Fuse time-series signals from process analytical technology (Raman, NIR, dielectric spectroscopy, dissolved oxygen, off-gas) with offline analytics. - Build mechanistic backbones (e.g., kinetic/ODE models, genome-scale metabolic models) that constrain learning and generate synthetic training data. - Develop machine learning surrogate models for computationally costly mechanistic simulations. - Quantify uncertainty so that models can be trusted in high-stakes production settings. Transfer across organisms and scales - Design models that carry over from benchtop to pilot and production scale, and across various microbes including bacteria and yeast. - Use transfer learning and representation learning to make good predictions for new strains and processes with little data. - Develop scale-transferable reactor characterisations and predictive KPI models for scale-up. Real-time Model-Predictive Control - Build the AI/ML layer for Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and reinforcement-learning-based feeding strategies to optimize titer, rate, and yield dynamically. - Fuse real-time data from Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and soft sensors (e.g., Raman, NIR) into dynamic state estimators to drive closed-loop bioreactor actuators (feed, air, agitation). - Prototype simpler, deployable steps along the way, such as deviation detection and operator alerts - Design control frameworks to proactively resolve metabolic bottlenecks and robustly account for model uncertainty, batch-to-batch variability, and inherent bioprocess stochasticity. QUALIFICATIONS: - PhD in machine learning, bioengineering, computational biology, or a related field, or a Master’s degree with 3+ years of relevant industry experience. - Strong research independence; ability to scope and execute novel scientific work from start to finish. - Demonstrated evidence of research contributions, including (but not limited to): peer-reviewed journal or conference papers, conference attendance, open-source contributions. - Strong Python and modern ML tooling (e.g., PyTorch/JAX, scikit-learn). - Hands-on experience building models of dynamical systems or time-series data, ideally combining mechanistic and data-driven approaches. - Experience working with frontier coding models, including multi-agent orchestration. - Clear written and verbal communication, including with non-ML partners. NICE-TO-HAVE: - Experience with bioprocess or fermentation data, ideally from bioreactors at more than one scale - Experience with Raman, NIR, or other spectroscopic data and chemometrics (e.g., PLS) - Background in model-predictive control, reinforcement learning, or optimal control - Experience with transfer learning, domain adaptation, or representation learning on biological data - Familiarity with genome-scale metabolic models or kinetic modelling - Experience with Bayesian methods, uncertainty quantification, or design of experiments - Experience in collaborative or publicly funded research projects (e.g. Horizon Europe, Eurostars) BENEFITS: - Competitive compensation through salary + stock options; we are looking to build a small but mighty team and think about compensation along those lines; - Build your research profile: Work on open problems with leading European academic and industrial partners, with the intention to present and publish your work; - A beautiful office in the heart of Munich, or remote work option with occasional travel - eGym WellPass membership

jobs.title: Doktorand*in (w/m/d) im Fachbereich der Biophysik
jobs.description: Über uns Das DWI – Leibniz-Institut für Interaktive Materialien ist eine von Bund und Ländern finanzierte Forschungseinrichtung der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft mit Sitz auf dem Campus Melaten der RWTH Aachen. Internationale Nachwuchswissenschaftler und erfahrene Wissenschaftler verschiedener Disziplinen entwickeln hier interaktive Materialien nach den Prinzipien der Natur. Es ist ein Ort, an dem Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Talenten, Erfahrungen und Kompetenzen zusammenarbeiten, um voneinander zu lernen und gemeinsam neues Wissen und neue Methoden für ein besseres Leben in unserer Welt zu schaffen. Position Das DWI sucht eine*n Doktorand*in (w/m/d) im Fachbereich der Biophysik die*der so bald wie möglich in der Forschungsgruppe von Dr. Charlotta Lorenz beginnen kann. Unsere Forschungsgruppe hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, weiche und biologische Materialien im Hinblick auf biomedizinische und nachhaltige Anwendungen zu erforschen und weiterzuentwickeln. Unser Schwerpunkt liegt insbesondere auf dem Zusammenspiel von Flüssig-Flüssig- oder Flüssig-Fest-Phasen in biologischen Materialien und darauf, wie sich die Eigenschaften dieser Materialien aus ihrer Struktur ergeben. So untersuchen wir beispielsweise flüssige, phasengetrennte Proteineinschlüsse in biologischen Polymernetzwerken und den Einfluss solcher Einschlüsse auf die Mechanik. Unsere Untersuchungen an phasentrennenden Proteinen könnten letztendlich zum Verständnis und zur Behandlung neurologischer Erkrankungen beitragen, an denen phasentrennende und aggregierende Proteine beteiligt sind. Im Bereich nachhaltiger Materialien kann die Phasentrennung als Konstruktionsprinzip dienen, um neue und stabile Strukturen zu bilden. Ihre Aufgaben Biologische Zellen sind hochkomplexe Systeme mit vielen miteinander interagierenden Komponenten. Ein schnell wachsendes Forschungsgebiet befasst sich mit der Phasentrennung von Proteinen in Biomolekularkondensate, die zahlreiche wesentliche Funktionen im Zellbetrieb erfüllen. Um den Zusammenhang zwischen Struktur und Funktion dieser Kondensate besser zu verstehen, zielt dieses Projekt darauf ab, ihre Struktur mithilfe von Streutechniken zu untersuchen. Da biomolekulare Kondensate bei neurologischen Erkrankungen eine Rolle spielen, können die Ergebnisse zu einem besseren Verständnis dieser Erkrankungen und langfristig möglicherweise auch zu deren Behandlung beitragen. In diesem Projekt werden wir die Struktur der Kondensate mithilfe verschiedener Techniken untersuchen, darunter Kleinwinkel-Röntgenstreuung, Neutronenstreuung, Lichtstreuung und Fluoreszenzmikroskopie. In der Anfangsphase werden die Proteine Rinderserumalbumin (BSA) und Fused-in-Sarcoma (FUS) als Modellsysteme für biomolekulare Kondensate verwendet. Sobald diese Systeme gut etabliert sind, werden weitere Proteinsysteme untersucht. Im Laufe des Projekts werden kleine Moleküle hinzugefügt, darunter Ionen, RNA und Chemikalien mit potenzieller Relevanz für neurologische Erkrankungen. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Verständnis struktureller Veränderungen während der Auflösung von Kondensaten. So wird beispielsweise erwartet, dass sich ein Protein wie FUS ausdehnt, wenn ein phasengetrenntes Tröpfchen kurz vor der Auflösung steht, doch könnte es sich auch ausdehnen, wenn das Tröpfchen stabilisiert wird. Die supramolekulare Anordnung phasengetrennter Proteine in solchen sich auflösenden Tröpfchen ist ebenfalls unbekannt und wird in diesem Projekt mittels SAXS untersucht. Das Projekt umfasst den Umgang mit Proteinen, standardmäßige Laborbiochemie, Strahlzeit-Experimente an Synchrotronen, Datenanalyse und den Vergleich mit physikalischen Modellen. jobs.description: Digitalisierung in der Batterieproduktion Über uns Das Institut für Werkzeugmaschinen und Betriebswissenschaften (iwb) der Technischen Universität München ist eines der großen produktionstechnischen Institute in Deutschland. Die Themenschwerpunkte umfassen die Bereiche Additive Fertigung, Batterieproduktion, Lasertechnik, Montagetechnik und Robotik, Nachhaltige Produktion, Produktionsmanagement und Logistik sowie Werkzeugmaschinen. In diesen Themenfeldern arbeiten die wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeitenden des iwb in Forschung, Lehre und Industrietransfer mit dem Ziel der Promotion abteilungsübergreifend zusammen. Anforderungen Überdurchschnittlich abgeschlossenes Masterstudium in einer der Fachrichtungen Maschinenbau, Physik, Informatik, Chemieingenieurwesen, Produktionstechnik oder in einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung Interesse an innovativen produktionstechnischen Fragestellungen und deren Untersuchung Spaß am experimentellen Arbeiten und der Betreuung von Versuchsanlagen Zielstrebigkeit und selbstständige Arbeitsweise Interesse an Projektmanagement und der Leitung von Forschungsprojekten Kreativität und Freude an experimentellen Arbeiten Ausgeprägte Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse (B2-Niveau) Aufgaben Eigenständige Bearbeitung von Forschungsprojekten, unter anderem zur Herstellung von Lithium-Ionen-Batteriezellen Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung digitaler Strukturen in der Pilotproduktion für Batteriezellen Analyse von Prozess- und Produktionsdaten zur Bewertung und Optimierung von Abläufen in der Batterieproduktion Implementierung und Evaluation von KI-Anwendungen in Prozessen der Batterieproduktion Eigenständige Bearbeitung von F&E-Projekten im Industrieauftrag Anleitung und Betreuung von Studierenden bei der Erstellung von Studien-/Abschlussarbeiten Betreuung von Lehrveranstaltungen aus dem Bereich der Produktionstechnik Wir bieten Vollzeitstelle als wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in mit der Möglichkeit zur Promotion Hochwertige Laborausstattung und neue Anlagentechnik für die Batterieproduktion Unterstützung durch nichtwissenschaftliche Mitarbeitende (sog. Service-Center, z. B. mechanische Werkstatt, IT, Verwaltung, Public Relations) Unterstützung für die Zeit nach der akademischen Karriere: Versuchsflächen und Büroräume für Start-ups, Bewerbungstraining, Pflege eines umfangreichen Alumni-Netzwerks durch den iwb e. V. Spannendes Forschungs- und Arbeitsumfeld inmitten eines engagierten Teams Industrienahe Forschung und kollaborative Zusammenarbeit mit Unternehmen unterschiedlicher Branchen Flexibles Arbeitszeitmodell mit Möglichkeit für Homeoffice Weitere Hinweise Die Beschäftigung erfolgt mit entsprechender Vergütung nach dem Tarifvertrag der Länder (TV-L). Schwerbehinderte Personen werden bei im Wesentlichen gleicher Eignung und Qualifikation bevorzugt eingestellt. Die TUM strebt eine Erhöhung des Frauenanteils an; Bewerbungen von Frauen werden daher ausdrücklich begrüßt. Beachten Sie bitte hierzu unsere Datenschutzhinweise gemäß Art. 13 der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) unter https://portal.mytum.de/kompass/datenschutz/Bewerbung/ zur Erhebung und Verarbeitung personenbezogener Daten im Rahmen Ihrer Bewerbung. jobs.title: ML Solution Consultant
jobs.location: New York, San Francisco, Munich or London
jobs.description: Thank you for your interest in Uncountable Implementations! ABOUT UNCOUNTABLE Science moves slowly — not because researchers aren't brilliant, but because their tools haven't kept up. Uncountable is changing that. We build a unified R&D platform used by the world's leading chemists, material scientists, and biologists to dramatically accelerate how new products are discovered, developed, and brought to market. Founded by engineers from MIT and Stanford, and trusted by enterprise R&D organizations across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, advanced materials, and food & beverage, Uncountable is on a mission to accelerate industrial R&D by an order of magnitude. We're a high-impact team that moves fast and gives people real ownership from day one. THE ROLE Machine learning is only as powerful as the people who can apply it in context — and in industrial R&D, that context is everything. As an ML Solution Consultant at Uncountable, you'll be the person who bridges deep technical expertise in data science and statistical modeling with a genuine understanding of how R&D scientists think, experiment, and make decisions. You'll work directly with leading R&D organizations to deploy Uncountable's AI capabilities, guiding customers through the full arc of adoption: from understanding their scientific challenges and data structures, to designing optimal experimentation strategies, to ensuring they're extracting real, measurable value from our platform's ML tools. This is not a back-office data science role. You'll be customer-facing, highly autonomous, and operating at the frontier of applied ML in science — advising PhD-level researchers and R&D directors on how to use AI to accelerate their most important work. You'll also have a direct line to product and engineering, shaping how our platform evolves based on what you see in the field. If you want to do meaningful applied ML work that reaches the real world — and have the communication skills to bring scientists along with you — this role is for you. WHAT YOU'LL DO Deploy AI Capabilities with Customers - Partner directly with R&D teams at enterprise customers to understand their scientific challenges, data environments, and experimentation workflows - Guide customers through onboarding onto Uncountable's ML tools, ensuring data is well-structured and models are configured to reflect their specific scientific context - Help customers interpret model outputs, act on recommendations, and build confidence in AI-driven experimentation over time Serve as a Technical and Scientific Expert - Act as a subject-matter expert in statistical modeling, machine learning, and experimental design — advising customers on strategies that maximize the value of their data - Translate complex ML concepts into clear, actionable guidance for scientists and R&D leaders who may not have a data science background - Troubleshoot modeling challenges, identify data quality issues, and design solutions that make the science work Drive Cross-Functional Impact - Collaborate closely with Uncountable's product and engineering teams, bringing structured customer feedback and real-world usage patterns to inform platform development - Identify recurring challenges and opportunities across customer engagements that can be addressed through new features or improved workflows - Contribute to internal knowledge-sharing on ML best practices, customer patterns, and domain-specific modeling approaches REQUIREMENTS - ML and data science depth: Strong foundation in machine learning, statistical modeling, or applied statistics — comfortable with experimental design, model evaluation, and working with messy, real-world scientific data - Scientific domain fluency: Experience working with R&D data, physical experimentation workflows, or scientific datasets — enough to speak credibly with researchers about their work - Communication: Exceptional ability to translate technical concepts into business and scientific value for a wide range of audiences, from bench scientists to R&D directors - Software fluency: Comfort working with data science tools and environments (Python, statistical software, or similar); experience with scientific or R&D software a strong plus - Autonomy: Ability to manage customer engagements independently, navigate ambiguity, and drive toward outcomes in a fast-paced environment PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - M.S. or Ph.D. in a quantitative field such as Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Physics, Data Science, or a closely related discipline - Experience in a customer-facing technical role — solutions engineering, technical consulting, or pre/post-sales data science - Exposure to product development processes in materials, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food science, or adjacent industries - Familiarity with Bayesian optimization, design of experiments (DoE), or active learning methods in applied settings WHY THIS ROLE - Applied ML that reaches the real world: Your work accelerates R&D at organizations developing next-generation products — from sustainable materials to life-saving medicines. The models you deploy aren't research artifacts; they're tools scientists use every day - Rare scope: You'll operate across scientific domains — coatings, polymers, pharmaceuticals, food science, advanced materials — developing breadth of expertise that's nearly impossible to build elsewhere - Scientific credibility meets technical depth: This role is built for people who can hold their own both in a conversation about experimental design with a PhD chemist and in a technical discussion with a product engineering team - Direct product influence: At our scale, what you learn in the field shapes what we build next. You'll have a real voice in Uncountable's ML roadmap - High autonomy, high impact: You'll own your customer relationships and drive outcomes — not execute a playbook BENEFITS - Competitive base salary with performance bonus and meaningful equity - Health and dental insurance - 401(k) with employer contribution (US locations) - Direct collaboration with a world-class engineering and data science team By applying for this role, your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Privacy Policy https://www.uncountable.com/privacy.

We build a unified R&D platform used by the world's leading chemists, material scientists, and biologists to dramatically accelerate how new products are discovered, developed, and brought to market. Founded by engineers from MIT and Stanford, and trusted by enterprise R&D organizations across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, advanced materials, and food & beverage, Uncountable is on a mission to accelerate industrial R&D by an order of magnitude. We're a high-impact team that moves fast and gives people real ownership from day one. THE ROLE This role is built for a scientist who is excited about what happens when good data infrastructure meets great research — and who wants to be on the front lines of making that happen. As a Scientific Implementation Associate, you'll work directly with R&D teams at some of the world's leading industrial companies, helping them bring their science into the Uncountable platform. That means understanding how they design experiments, what data they generate, and how they think about their workflows — then translating all of that into a platform configuration that actually reflects their science. It's hands-on, technically engaging work. You'll spend time restructuring and contextualizing real customer datasets, designing data models that capture complex experimental relationships, and iterating on configurations in close collaboration with scientists and engineers. Over time, you'll also take on increasing ownership of full customer implementations — from first meeting through go-live. This is an ideal entry point for someone with a scientific background who wants to build a career at the intersection of science, software, and customer impact — without leaving their domain expertise behind. WHAT YOU'LL DO Support Scientific Implementations - Work alongside senior implementation team members to onboard new customers and support existing ones with new implementation initiatives - Learn and apply Uncountable's implementation methodology to configure the platform for individual customers' experimental workflows and data environments - Take on increasing ownership of implementations over time, eventually leading your own from end to end Design and Configure Complex Scientific Workflows - Translate customers' experimental paradigms — how they define formulations, design experiments, record measurements, and track results — into accurate, well-structured platform configurations - Map scientific data structures (multi-variable formulations, hierarchical sample relationships, linked test methods) onto Uncountable's data model, making principled decisions about how to best represent each customer's science - Work through ambiguous, real-world data environments — customers with years of legacy spreadsheets, idiosyncratic naming conventions, and non-standard workflows — and design configurations that are both scientifically accurate and practically usable - Iterate on platform configurations in working sessions with customers, testing and refining until the system genuinely reflects how their team thinks about their research Engage Directly with Customers - Join and eventually lead meetings with R&D scientists, data managers, and technical stakeholders - Build credibility through scientific fluency — understanding customers' domains well enough to ask the right questions and propose the right solutions - Communicate clearly and empathetically across a wide range of audiences, from bench scientists to R&D directors Contribute to Team Knowledge - Help document reusable configuration patterns across domains (coatings, polymers, pharma, food science, etc.) that accelerate future implementations - Share observations from the field with product and engineering teams to help shape what Uncountable builds next YOUR FIRST 180 DAYS Month 1: Develop deep fluency in Uncountable's platform and implementation methodology. Begin configuring experimental data for onboarded customers under the guidance of senior team members, learning how to faithfully capture end-user workflows. Months 2–3: Start joining customer meetings and demos, contributing to scientific due diligence sessions and data requirement conversations. Take on configuration work more independently, with support from your team. Months 4–6: Take ownership of the implementation process for a new customer. Lead meetings, set timelines, manage milestones, and advocate for any product development needed to deliver a great outcome. REQUIREMENTS - Scientific background: A B.S. or higher in chemistry, materials science, biology, chemical engineering, or a related field — or 1+ years of hands-on experience in a scientific or technical role - Data fluency: Comfort working with data in Excel or similar tools; Python or other scripting skills are a significant plus - Software fluency: Hands-on comfort working with scientific or technical software — whether that's an ELN, LIMS, instrument software, or data analysis tools. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be someone who picks up new tools quickly and isn't intimidated by data-heavy environments - Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to varied audiences - Empathy and adaptability: The ability to understand not just what a scientist is saying, but what they actually need — and to adapt to different organizational styles and working environments - Curiosity: A genuine interest in software, data, and how technology can transform R&D workflows PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Hands-on lab experience — time spent running experiments gives you instant credibility with our customers - Exposure to data management concepts: structured spreadsheets, databases, ELNs, or LIMS - Experience in a customer-facing, teaching, or collaborative technical role - Familiarity with more than one scientific domain (e.g., organic chemistry and polymer science, or biotech and formulation) - Python or scripting experience for data processing or analysis WHY THIS ROLE - A rare entry point: This role gives scientists a path into the tech industry that doesn't require abandoning their domain expertise — you'll use your scientific knowledge every day, and deepen it across new fields - Fast ownership: We give people real responsibility early. Within six months, you'll be leading your own customer implementations — not just supporting them - Direct impact: Your work accelerates R&D at organizations developing next-generation products, from sustainable materials to pediatric cancer treatments - Clear career growth: Previous Scientific Implementation Associates at Uncountable have grown into Manager and Director-level roles, with exposure across scientific domains, enterprise software, and business development - An engineering-first culture: You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams, giving you a window into how world-class software gets built — and a voice in shaping it BENEFITS - Competitive base salary with performance bonus and equity - Health and dental insurance - 401(k) with employer contribution (US locations) - Direct mentorship from experienced implementation managers and a fast path to increased ownership By applying for this role, your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Privacy Policy https://www.uncountable.com/privacy.

jobs.title: Implementation Lead / Program Manager
jobs.location: New York, San Francisco, Munich or London
jobs.description: Thank you for your interest in Uncountable Implementations! ABOUT UNCOUNTABLE Science moves slowly, not because researchers aren't brilliant, but because their tools haven't kept up. Uncountable is changing that. We build a unified R&D platform used by leading chemists, material scientists, and biologists to speed up how new products are discovered, developed, and brought to market. Founded by engineers from MIT and Stanford, and trusted by enterprise R&D organizations across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, advanced materials, and food & beverage, Uncountable is on a mission to accelerate industrial R&D by an order of magnitude. We're a high-impact team that moves fast and gives people real ownership from day one. THE ROLE As an Implementation Program Manager, you own a customer's implementation from scoping to go-live, across every phase. You are the person the customer's R&D leadership looks to for the plan, the timeline, and the answer to "where are we?" Inside Uncountable, you are the person the delivery team looks to for direction. Each implementation runs with a defined team. Account Managers own the customer relationship, adoption, and growth. Scientific Implementation Managners own the technical design. Scientific Implementation team members execute the build, working heavily with AI agents that handle repetitive configuration and setup. The Implementation Program Manager sits at the center: you own the project management and make sure the whole team delivers what was scoped, on time and within hours. This is not a pure project management role. You need enough scientific and platform depth to scope a lab's real workflows, push back on a design that won't hold up, and earn the trust of PhD-level researchers. You also need the operating discipline to run status, stage gates, and sign-offs on several enterprise accounts at once. If you have led scientific software rollouts, or run implementations as a consultant, and want to do it with a modern, AI-first delivery team, this is that role. WHAT YOU'LL DO Own the implementation, scoping to go-live - Lead scoping with the customer: define requirements, sites, teams, and workflows in and out of each phase, and agree on what a realistic first go-live includes - Turn scoping into a phased plan with a timeline, deliverables, and post-sales commitments the delivery team can execute against - Own on-time go-live for every phase and the hours spent against what was scoped Run the project - Run status meetings with the customer and internally, and keep a current, written status the AM and leadership can read without asking - Manage stage gates and customer sign-offs, so each phase closes cleanly before the next one opens - Plan and run onsites and workshops, from agenda and logistics to who attends from both sides - Spot scope creep and overruns early, and raise change requests or resourcing asks with clear justification rather than absorbing them quietly Drive integrations and cross-team work - Scope integration requirements with the customer's IT and business teams, and write tickets the Integration Engineering team can act on - Coordinate the enterprise integrations that a go-live depends on, such as sending data to ERP or other enterprise systems - Work with implementation partners and system integrators when a customer brings one, and hold the delivery to Uncountable's standard Lead the delivery team on your accounts - Manager the work of the Scientific Implementation Managers & Associates on each account: who does what, by when - Push SIs and the team to use AI agents for configuration and setup, and keep people working on the parts that need judgment - Bring forward what you learn across accounts, so scoping, estimates, and playbooks get better for the next implementation Partner with the Account Manager - Keep the AM informed on progress, risks, and customer sentiment, and escalate to them when an issue needs an executive conversation - Sequence future phases jointly with the AM, for example deciding when to bring the next R&D team onto the platform - Hand off to the AM and Customer Success at go-live with a clear picture of what was delivered and what comes next YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS Month 1: Learn the Uncountable platform and how we implement it, including the AI agents our SIs use for configuration. Shadow live implementations at different stages: a scoping workshop, a mid-build status cycle, and a go-live. Get to know the AMs, Solution Architects, and SIs you will work with. Month 2: Take over project management on one or two live implementations at their next phase boundary. Run status meetings and stage gates, own the written status, and take on integration scoping and onsite planning from the AM. Month 3: Own a new implementation end to end: lead scoping, set the phased plan and timeline, staff the team with your manager, and run it toward its first go-live. Bring at least one concrete improvement to how we scope, estimate, or report on implementations. REQUIREMENTS - Implementation leadership: 3+ years leading software implementations or digital lab rollouts, whether for external clients at a vendor or consultancy, or internally as the project lead who brought an ELN, LIMS, or similar platform into your own R&D organization. At least a few of these should be ones where you owned the plan, the stakeholders, and the outcome end to end - Scientific grounding: A background in chemistry, materials science, biology, chemical engineering, or a related field, enough to scope R&D workflows and hold your own with PhD-level researchers - Project discipline: You run status, risks, scope, and sign-offs as a habit, across several concurrent projects, without being chased for it - Ownership and judgment: You push back when a timeline, scope, or design doesn't make sense, including with customers and senior colleagues, and you take responsibility for the result - AI-first working style: You already use AI tools in your own work and want a team where agents do a real share of the build. You will be expected to drive their adoption on your accounts - Communication: Clear, concise writing and presenting for audiences from bench scientists to R&D directors and IT leaders - Pace: Comfortable in a fast-moving company where processes are still being built and you help build them PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - M.S. or Ph.D. in a scientific or engineering field - Experience implementing or rolling out ELN, LIMS, PLM, or other R&D data platforms, either on the vendor side or as the customer's project lead - Experience leading digital initiatives across several sites or regions, including on-site workshops with scientific teams - Experience scoping integrations with ERP or other enterprise systems, and working with IT organizations NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS - Experience working with or managing implementation partners and system integrators - Experience in a regulated or GxP-adjacent environment - A second language used by our customers, such as German, French, or Spanish WHY THIS ROLE - Real ownership: You are the named owner of the implementation on accounts that include some of the largest R&D organizations in chemicals, consumer goods, and pharma - A new delivery model: You will help define how a modern implementation team works when agents do a large share of the configuration, and your input will shape the playbook - Breadth: Coatings, polymers, food science, pharma, and more, often in the same week - Internal influence: What you see across accounts feeds directly into how we scope, price, and staff implementations, and into what product builds next - Room to grow: The role sits close to delivery leadership, with a path to leading a group of Implementation Program Managers or a larger part of the delivery organization as the team grows BENEFITS - Competitive base salary with performance bonus and meaningful equity - Health and dental insurance - 401(k) with employer contribution (US locations) - Direct exposure to company leadership on a small, high-caliber team By applying for this role, your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Privacy Policy https://www.uncountable.com/privacy.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION - Work on some of the most critical physics challenges that govern the conceptual viability and optimal performance of steady state fusion reactors. - Advance the next generation of edge transport physics models (including turbulent transport characterisation, drift effects, and impurity migration) required for reactor-relevant stellarator exhaust solutions. - Apply state-of-the-art numerical models directly to hardware design decisions with reactor-scale impact. - Contribute to the European initiative leading the critical path to a fusion power plant. - Work alongside talented, mission-driven experts in a supportive, ambitious environment that is building real devices, not just reactor concepts. Grounded in experimental validation and integrated with engineering constraints, your work will directly inform the design of next-generation plasma exhaust systems for commercial fusion. This is an opportunity to turn frontier edge physics into reactor-ready solutions and help close the gap between today’s modelling capability and the needs of fusion power. WHAT YOU WILL DO - As an edge transport physicist at Proxima, you will play a central role in efforts to model and design the edge and Scrape-Off Layer of real-world machines that are necessary steps on the path towards commercial fusion power. - You will develop and apply theoretical and computational models that surpass the state of the art, closing key gaps in turbulent transport, equilibrium ExB flows, molecular recombination, and impurity behaviour in the stellarator edge. - Your results and design strategy will be grounded by experimental insights, before being integrated into the design of next generation plasma exhaust systems. - Your work will involve close engagement with engineers to ensure compatibility with overall device design and reactor-relevant operating scenarios. Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach. Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions. BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO - Shape the architecture of a fusion power plant – Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale. - Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges – Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product. - Design real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world – Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy. YOUR IMPACT Alpha will be the first stellarator to demonstrate net energy. Achieving this milestone requires building a deeply coupled machine, where plasma, magnets, structures, cryogenics, and heating work at the edge of each discipline’s capability. As part of the integrated stellarator design team you will work in between plasma physics and technology and make sure that all stellarator systems are designed according to clear and optimal design criteria. You will ensure that modelling uncertainties are quantified and used appropriately. You will drive projects where overarching design solutions with multi-system trades need to be found. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Ensure interfaces, design criteria, load cases and uncertainties are correctly defined: so that engineering design can iterate quickly and with clear assumptions. - Understand systems interactions: in order to minimize unintended consequences of the main architectural decisions. - Solve integration challenges: Identify, track, and solve the hardest integration challenges and risks of a machine not achieving its mission requirements. - Harness simplification opportunities: Identify, track, and address the most promising opportunities that affect the Alpha architecture. WHO YOU ARE - You've earned your engineering judgment on complex machines. You hold a PhD or Master's in physics, engineering, or an adjacent field, and you have years of experience in industries where integration challenges are at the heart of the design, such as aerospace or Formula 1. - You are not afraid of different physics domains. You feel comfortable navigating the different physics regimes of a Stellarator - from waves propagating in a plasma to cryogenic properties of steel. - You reach for whatever tool fits. Being a pen-and-paper calculation, a simulator you coded last night, or a commercial multiphysics package, the method serves the question, never the reverse. - You build consensus. You are a low-ego high-clarity communicator who works effectively with multiple technical leads, to bring integration challenges and system-level tradeoffs to a clear decision. - You commit to a concrete outcome. Every study, tool, and memo you produce ends in an actionable insight and a clear next step, otherwise it didn't happen. WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION - You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world. - You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals. - Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey. - Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent. YOUR IMPACT You will make Proxima's plasma simulation stack trustworthy by confronting it with reality. Every prediction we make for Alpha – Proxima's Q>1 experimental stellarator – and for Stellaris, our commercial power plant, rests on models whose credibility has to be earned against real measurements from an operating device. W7-X is where we earn it. You will take our integrated modeling framework, FUS3, and our Bayesian plasma state estimation workflow to W7-X data: reconstruct the plasma state from diagnostic measurements, compare our predictive models against what the machine actually did, and turn the discrepancies into a prioritized map of where our physics is right, where it is not, and what we must fix before Alpha's first plasma. Modeling sits on Alpha's operational critical path and cannot be backfilled after first plasma – this role is how we get ahead of it. You will be the person in the group who lives at the intersection of modeling and experiment: fluent enough in the physics to know what a model should predict, and close enough to the diagnostics to know what the data can actually support. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Validate Proxima's predictive plasma models against W7-X experimental data – neoclassical and turbulent transport, 3D equilibrium, ECRH deposition, pellet fueling and drift, bootstrap current and iota evolution – and record each comparison as a reproducible validation report with quantitative agreement metrics, stated limitations, and a pinned regression test - Reconstruct the plasma state from real diagnostic measurements using our time-dependent Bayesian state-estimation workflow (Thomson scattering, interferometry, CXRS, ECE, XICS, bolometry, magnetics), with calibrated uncertainties, and benchmark it against established analyses such as Minerva/IDA reconstructions and ASTRA power-balance results - Work with raw and pre-processed diagnostic data, not just analyzed profiles – instrument geometry, sightlines, calibrations and the caveats that come with them – and own the forward models, noise models and profile fits that feed transport analysis - Validate against databases of discharges rather than single shots, across W7-X magnetic configurations and operating regimes, so the output is a map of model applicability and parameter trends rather than one-off discrepancy reports - Act as a technical interface to W7-X and IPP: scope and prioritize data requests, spend time on site in Greifswald working alongside diagnosticians and operators, and propose and support experiments that directly target our model gaps - Feed validation back into design – convert diagnostic placement and observability studies on W7-X into requirements for Alpha's diagnostic set, and into realistic uncertainty models for the synthetic measurements we use to design against - Extend the modeling stack itself: mappers from experimental archives into IMAS, synthetic diagnostics, and analysis workflows, so that interpreting a shot end-to-end – raw data to reconstructed plasma state to physics quantities – runs in minutes and is reproducible by anyone in the group - As Alpha approaches operation, help stand up the between-shot analysis loop that will run on day one WHO YOU ARE - PhD in plasma physics, fusion science, or a closely related discipline - Hands-on experience with experimental data from a magnetic confinement device – you have dealt with diagnostics, calibrations, systematic errors, and all the ways real data is messier than simulation output - Experience reconstructing the plasma state from measurements: profile fitting, integrated data analysis, equilibrium reconstruction, or power and particle balance analysis - Strong grounding in transport, equilibrium, and heating physics – enough to tell a code bug from a physics discovery - Rigorous about uncertainty; you treat a validation claim without error bars on both sides as incomplete - Comfortable writing and maintaining scientific software – version control, testing, and reproducibility are habits, not overhead - Can communicate effectively with physicists, diagnosticians, engineers, and experimentalists, and work productively inside an external collaboration - Self-directed; able to identify what needs to be done and execute - Willing to travel regularly to Greifswald, and later to the Alpha site NICE TO HAVE - W7-X experience - operations, diagnostics, or data analysis, and familiarity with the W7-X data archive and Minerva - Stellarator physics background - Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification, or machine learning applied to experimental data - Experience with integrated modeling and transport codes (FUSE, OMFIT, ASTRA, TRANSP, FUSE, JINTRAC, or similar) and with neoclassical (SFINCS, DKES, NEO) or gyrokinetic (GENE, CGYRO, GX, or similar) codes -
